description: Ranked search over one public table's rows, the same search its dataset page runs: words, prefixes, typos and spelling correction, served from the table's search package. NOT a catalogue search (search_datasets finds datasets) and not SQL. Example: {"table_id": "0f2f...", "query": "blade runner 1982"}. settled defaults to true (a finished query, which may be planned by a model); send settled: false for a fast keystroke answer planned by the parser alone. page_size is 1-100 (default 20). columns is a subset of the table's search display columns (default all of them). Returns {rows: [{row_id, fields}], plan, planner, retrieval, next_cursor, count, package: {generation_id, package_digest}, table_version_id, timings}. For the next page send the same query with the answer's plan and next_cursor. like: a row_id from an answer finds the rows most like that row (more like this; query, when not empty, is a topic beside it), on a table whose search has meaning vectors. mode (first page only): auto (default) lets the planner choose; meaning ranks by meaning alone; image finds rows whose pictures look like the query (posters showing a red sky over a city); emoji searches by the query's emojis. Most tables search words only. like and the meaning and image modes need meaning vectors, which a table has only when capabilities.search.semantic_columns from get_table_schema is not empty. When it is empty, use the default mode. A table whose search cannot run a mode answers invalid_plan. count: true also asks for the exact number of matching rows; count is null when the table cannot count yet. corrected, when present, is the spelling the search used. Find the table with search_datasets and list_tables, then check that get_table_schema returns capabilities.search. A table with no ready search answers search_unavailable with a reason: preparing (after a publisher activates search this can last minutes, and longer on a large table; the answer carries retry_after_seconds, so retry once that wait has passed), not_public (another workspace's private or link-shared table; your own workspace's tables are searchable whatever their visibility) or the package's state. To filter, sort or aggregate, use query_table. No key needed on a public table: a keyless caller gets 30 calls a minute and 600 a day per address, and 300 a minute and 10,000 a day across all keyless callers, and settled calls share the dataset page's per-table limit. A refusal past that answers rate_limited with retry_after_seconds. Without a key, private and link-shared tables, and public tables whose publisher turned download off, answer table_not_available. An mr_use_ workspace key (Authorization: Bearer) or an OAuth connection lifts the limit to the key's query limit (60 calls a minute per key or connection, shared with query_table, and 5,000 a day per workspace) and adds the workspace's own tables. A keyed call counts against the workspace's allowance, as query_table does. Cite the package generation and digest.
name: search_table
title: Search a table's rows
